# RankFence

RankFence is an MIT-licensed Python coordinator for exact reciprocal rank fusion of ranked result streams. Its distinctive integration is a trusted map of disjoint search namespaces. It can cancel all pending reads on a losing shard before the global answer is ready. Requires Python 3.10+. No runtime dependencies or API key.

- Guide and contract: https://pgg-engineering-rankfence.static.hf.space/guide.html
- Try privately in a browser: https://pgg-engineering-rankfence.static.hf.space/workbench.html
- Baselines, counterexamples and reproducibility: https://pgg-engineering-rankfence.static.hf.space/benchmarks.html
- Install: python -m pip install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgg898200-ship-it/streamsieve/9107326cf0993e842c281d412cb276e83eb1c6a4/releases/rankfence-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
- All Python source, tests, replay scripts and original result files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgg898200-ship-it/streamsieve/9107326cf0993e842c281d412cb276e83eb1c6a4/releases/rankfence-0.1.0.zip

## When does it fit?

Stable, pull-based ranked cursors. Each source contributes 1/(c+rank), starting at rank one. Fuse rankings synchronously with PartitionFence or asynchronously with fuse_partitioned. An ID may appear in multiple retrievers within one group. The application must guarantee it cannot appear in multiple groups. Use Fence or fuse when ID overlap across groups is unknown. Weighted RRF and mutable or reordered prefixes require other products or scoring contracts. Whole-window retrieval can be faster when a backend precomputes a cheap ranking.

## Evidence

On 100 Robust03 topics hash-split into eight simulated shards, retirement consumed 78,956 of 400,000 input IDs. A wrapper that independently resolved every shard with RankSeal and merged scores consumed 206,934 IDs. All ordered top fives agreed. A support-aware integer baseline matched the 82,637 reads of RankFence with retirement disabled. No production latency or market-share claims.

- Raw shard comparison: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgg898200-ship-it/streamsieve/9107326cf0993e842c281d412cb276e83eb1c6a4/results/rankseal.json
- Real SQLite FTS5 example results: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgg898200-ship-it/streamsieve/9107326cf0993e842c281d412cb276e83eb1c6a4/results/sqlite-fts.json
- Unpartitioned replay: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgg898200-ship-it/streamsieve/9107326cf0993e842c281d412cb276e83eb1c6a4/results/robust03.json

## Local MCP tools

After installing the wheel, a stdio MCP client can launch `python -m rankfence.mcp`. rankfence_analyze replays a bounded materialized query with the supplied shard map. rankfence_verify checks a receipt. Input payloads stay in the local process.

- Product source and tested MCP request: https://github.com/pgg898200-ship-it/streamsieve/tree/rankfence-v0.1.0#let-an-agent-measure-its-own-workload
